function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Below is a quick‑look guide to the **next major festivals happening in the United States** after today (June 22 2026).  The list is sorted by the earliest start date, and it covers a mix of music, cultural, food, and family‑friendly events.  For the most up‑to‑date ticket prices, lineup announcements, and travel tips, be sure to visit each festival’s official website or a trusted ticket‑reseller.

| # | Festival | Dates (2026) | Location | Type | Highlights |
|---|----------|--------------|----------|------|-------------|
| 1 | **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** | **April 14–16 & April 21–23** | Indio, California (Coachella Valley) | Music & Arts | 20+ stages, top‑tier headliners, art installations, fashion, and immersive experiences. |
| 2 | **Newport Folk Festival** | **May 12–15** | Newport, Rhode Island | Folk / Americana | 100+ artists, historic waterfront setting, family‑friendly programming. |
| 3 | **Austin City Limits Music Festival** | **May 26–29** | Austin, Texas | Music | 3‑day, 30+ stages, indie, rock, hip‑hop, and country acts. |
| 4 | **Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival** | **June 9–12** | Manchester, Tennessee | Music & Arts | 30+ stages, eclectic line‑up, camping, art, and wellness workshops. |
| 5 | **Summerfest** | **June 15–19** | Milwaukee, Wisconsin | Music | 8‑day, 200+ stages, 400+ acts, “World’s Largest Music Festival.” |
| 6 | **Lollapalooza** | **July 7–10** | Chicago, Illinois | Music | 4‑day, 30+ stages, mainstream & indie acts, food trucks, and art installations. |
| 7 | **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | **July 15–18** | New Orleans, Louisiana | Jazz & Heritage | 4‑day, 200+ stages, jazz, blues, zydeco, Cajun, and world music. |
| 8 | **Burning Man** | **August 28–September 6** | Black Rock Desert, Nevada | Art & Culture | 10‑day, 1,000+ participants, art installations, community, and self‑expression. |
| 9 | **South by Southwest (SXSW)** | **March 11–20** | Austin, Texas | Music, Film & Interactive | 10‑day, 500+ artists, film premieres, tech demos, networking. |
|10 | **Taste of Chicago** | **August 4–7** | Chicago, Illinois | Food & Culture | 4‑day, 200+ food vendors, live music, cooking demos, and family activities. |

### How to Pick the Right Festival for You

| Factor | What to Look For |
|--------|------------------|
| **Genre** | Are you into rock, hip‑hop, folk, electronic, or a mix? |
| **Location** | Do you prefer a city vibe, a desert, a beach, or a rural setting? |
| **Duration** | 1‑day events are great for a quick trip; multi‑day festivals often require camping. |
| **Line‑up** | Check the official lineup announcements; early‑bird tickets often lock in your favorite acts. |
| **Tickets & Camping** | Early‑bird tickets usually include camping; later tickets may be limited or sold out. |
| **Travel & Accommodation** | Book flights/hotels early; many festivals have official partner hotels. |
| **Accessibility & Family‑Friendly** | Some festivals have dedicated kids’ zones, while others are strictly adult‑only. |

### Quick Tips for Attending a Festival

1. **Buy Tickets Early** – Most festivals sell out months in advance.  
2. **Plan Your Travel** – Use public transit, carpool, or rideshare to avoid parking hassles.  
3. **Pack Smart** – Bring a reusable water bottle, sunscreen, a light jacket, and a portable phone charger.  
4. **Stay Hydrated & Eat Well** – Many festivals now offer healthy food options and hydration stations.  
5. **Know the Rules** – Check each festival’s policy on outside food, photography, and prohibited items.  
6. **Explore Beyond the Stages** – Art installations, workshops, and local vendors add extra layers of fun.  

---

#### Next Festival to Watch

If you’re looking for the **very next festival** after today, it’s **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** (April 14–16 & April 21–23).  It’s one of the most iconic U.S. festivals, and tickets usually go on sale in late September/early October of the previous year.  Keep an eye on the official Coachella website for lineup updates and ticket release dates.

Happy festival hunting! 🎶🌟
